title: In situ Atomic-Scale Imaging Unveils Clamping-Enhanced Strain and Phase Transition Pathways in Antiferroelectric Thin Films
content: Antiferroelectric thin films hold transformative potential for next-generation micro- and nano-electromechanical systems [1], yet their atomic-scale phase transition dynamics under operational conditions remain largely unresolved [2, 3]. In this study [4], we employ in situ and operando scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) to directly visualize the structural evolution of epitaxial PbZrO3 (PZO) thin films during electric-field-driven phase transitions. By integrating nano-beam electron diffraction (NBED) with atomic-resolution imaging, we reveal how substrate clamping and defect-mediated phase pathways synergize to amplify electromechanical performance.
